title: Client interop adapters for granular rollback and eventual-consistency guarantees
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Summary: Build a thin, cross-language client adapter layer (Python/TypeScript/Go) that lets applications tolerate mixed server and client SDK versions during a rollout, provide deterministic rollback semantics for paginated/streaming flows, and maintain eventual consistency guarantees for idempotent operations. This PRD focuses on behavioral contracts, acceptance criteria, and an incremental rollout strategy that minimizes server-side changes.

Problem: During previous rollouts we observed clients failing to resume pagination or streaming sessions when server-side pagination cursors or streaming framing changed. This forced immediate rollbacks or customer remediation. There is no standardized shim that provides safe compatibility transitions across SDK versions, particularly when customers use long-lived cursors, tokenized pagination, or resumable streams with interleaved writes.

Goals:
- Provide adapters in Python/TS/Go that implement graceful downgrade and rollback behavior with minimal application changes.
- Ensure paginated iterators and streaming consumers can detect incompatible frames and fall back to safe full-reload or server-replay strategies.
- Define idempotency and cursor semantics so clients and servers can agree on consistency windows.
- Ship with a staged rollout and feature-flag support to validate behavior across customers.

Non-goals:
- This work will not change server-side token formats; aim is to adapt clients to tolerate changes while server teams coordinate versioned cursors.
- Not covering major protocol rewrites or binary-compat kernel changes; those are separate infra projects.

Stakeholders: PM (Sofia Chen), Eng Lead (Miguel Ruiz), SDK owners (Python: Asha Patel; TS: Liam O'Connor; Go: Priya Nair), Security (Ravi Desai), Design (Marina Lopez).

Risks:
- Additional client-side complexity could increase SDK surface area and maintenance burden.
- Subtle edge cases around concurrent operations and eventual consistency windows may lead to rare duplication or missed items if not rigorously tested.

Success metrics:
- Reduce rollback-triggered outages during SDK rollouts by 90% compared to baseline.
- No more than 1% of active pagination/streaming users experience unrecoverable resume failures during canary.
- CPU/memory overhead from adapters <5% in common client scenarios.
technical_requirements: Provide a language-consistent adapter package for Python, TypeScript, and Go with identical semantics exposed in idiomatic APIs
Adapters expose a feature flag and opt-in compatibility mode: 'compat-v1' that enables retry/downgrade pathways
Paginated iterators must implement 'safe_rewind' and 'full_replay' fallbacks when cursor validation fails
Streaming consumers must detect incompatible frames (version mismatch, header mismatch) and trigger resumable replay or switch to checkpointed polling
Idempotency token API: optional client-supplied idempotency key for write actions that interact with pagination or stream checkpoints
All adapters log deterministic diagnostic events (compat.check, compat.fallback, compat.rollback) with trace ids for correlation
Low-level wire/backwards compatibility: prefer non-breaking server headers; adapters should only parse headers, not rely on cursor payload shape
Compatibility shim should be shipped as a separately importable module to avoid increasing default SDK size for users who opt-out
Expose explicit migration helpers: validate_cursor(cursor) and adapt_cursor_for_server(cursor) to help customers diagnose issues
Provide a no-op path for older SDKs to avoid regressions when customers do not opt into compatibility mode
api_examples:
Python: from redwood_sdk.compat import CompatIter
with CompatIter(client.list_items(pagination=True), mode="compat-v1") as it:
    for page in it:
        process(page)
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for adapter behaviors in Python/TS/Go covering: cursor validation failure, partial page replays, stream frame fallback, idempotent write deduplication
Integration tests against a compatibility testbed that can simulate: cursor rotation, header mismatch, partial replay and out-of-order frames
Performance benchmark showing <5% median latency regression for paginated list flows when adapter enabled in a common SDK configuration
Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic with observability dashboards showing compat.check, compat.fallback metrics and error heatmaps
Rollback plan validated in staging: toggling feature flag off should return behavior to baseline with no persistent state corruption
Documentation for migration helpers and sample migration guides published to docs.redwood.com
Sign-off from Security for idempotency key handling and KMS recommendations for sensitive cursor material
testing_plan: Unit test matrix across languages and runtime versions (Python 3.9-3.11, Node 16-20, Go 1.20-1.22)
Integration test harness: launch server stub that can inject header/cursor faults and capture client events
Chaos tests that randomly rotate cursors mid-iteration and validate adapter fallbacks do not double-count items
End-to-end canary against 5% production customers with synthetic test accounts simulating long-lived cursors
Load test to verify adapter memory characteristics and absence of leak under high-concurrency iterators
Security review on idempotency key flows and telemetry to ensure no PII leakage
migration_plan: Phase 1: Release adapters as opt-in packages and document migration steps. Phase 2: Instrument a small subset of SDK consumers (internal apps + 10 customers) and iterate on observed failure modes. Phase 3: Expand canary to 25% and provide 'migration helper' scripts to customers. Phase 4: Enabled by default for new SDK installs and opt-out for legacy installs for one quarter before full default flip. Backout: server can disable compat header handling and clients will revert to baseline when feature flag toggled off.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only SDK builds + developer playground tests (2 weeks)
Beta: external canary on a small customer set + telemetry + weekly check-ins (3 weeks)
Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over four weeks with automated health gates
GA: default enabled for new installs after 8 weeks and announced migration window
Kill-switch: global feature flag in Console with immediate disable and automatic instrumentation snapshot
observability_and_metrics: compat.check.count: number of times adapters validate a cursor/header
compat.rollback.count: number of rollbacks initiated by client adapters
adapter.latency.p50/p95 for paginated next() and streaming read()
customer.failure_rate: per-customer rate of unrecoverable resume failures
memory.per_iterator: observable gauge to detect leaks
implementation_notes: Prefer small helper libraries that can be vendored into existing SDKs to avoid large refactors
Coordinate with Runtime/Serving teams to standardize a 'Compat-Version' HTTP header we can read while keeping header optional
Encrypt cursor artifacts where possible; if cursor contains sensitive payload, recommend server publish opaque handle and server-side validation
Add structured telemetry events with trace ids to expedite post-mortem debugging
Document clear semantic expectations: adapters only change read/iterate semantics; they do not alter server-side data ordering guarantees
notes: Design feedback (2025-03-05): Marina requested explicit UX for back-off behavior in streaming adapters; added to acceptance criteria
Security note (2025-03-07): Ravi asked for KMS guidance for any cursor signing/encryption; security review added
Engineering estimate (2025-03-09): Initial implementation 6-8 sprints across three SDK teams to reach beta; parallel work recommended across languages
Follow-up: schedule a cross-team sync with Serving (ENG-94211) to standardize header names and corner-case semantics
